stage: private beta landing page plus clickable prototype
audience: busy solo travelers planning two-to-five day city trips
business_goal: collect ten qualified beta users without confusing first-time visitors
review_goal: decide what to fix before sharing the app in a community post
constraints: No payment flow is live yet
Owner has one weekend to make changes
Owner wants practical product feedback, not a full redesign

screens.name: Landing page hero
screens.user_question: What does this do for me in the next five minutes?
friction_points: Headline says smarter travel planning but does not name the output
No example itinerary appears above the fold
Primary action and secondary action compete visually
screens.evidence: Three test readers described the app as a generic travel blog.

screens.name: Trip preference form
screens.user_question: How much work is required before I see value?
friction_points: Form asks for twelve fields before showing an example
No privacy note explains what happens to travel preferences
screens.evidence: Prototype testers paused at the budget field and asked what data was saved.

screens.name: Generated itinerary screen
screens.user_question: Can I trust and edit this plan?
friction_points: Restaurants and activities have no source links
No warning when an activity may be closed on selected dates
Edit controls are hidden below the generated plan
screens.evidence: Testers liked the plan but asked how to verify hours and swap activities.

readiness_checks.criterion: Visitor can understand the product in one sentence
readiness_checks.notes: Value prop is abstract and does not show the generated artifact.

readiness_checks.criterion: Visitor sees proof before being asked to commit
readiness_checks.notes: No itinerary preview, before/after, or example route appears early.
Sources, date checks, and edit controls need to be visible.

readiness_checks.criterion: Owner has a small next experiment
readiness_checks.notes: A 10-person beta with a clearer landing page is reasonable.
